provenance.method: ran the reference hash_source in a source-checkout venv
provenance.why_here: a build worktree has no Python environment and cannot run the reference, so it cannot produce these

hash_source_file.note: FILE: sha256 of the file's CONTENTS

hash_source_directory.note: DIRECTORY: NOT a content hash. sha256 of newline-joined sorted 'relpath:size' over rglob files. A deliberate speed tradeoff; an implementation that 'improves' it to a content hash silently stops matching every manifest already on an owner's disk.
hash_source_directory.algorithm: sha256('\n'.join(f'{rel}:{size}' for f in sorted(path.rglob('*')) if f.is_file()))

falsification.note: the property a content-hash port would break; BOTH must hold

reference_written_manifest.note: written by the reference write_manifest(). READ-OLD fixture: the native scanner must find this by its source_hash. Field set and value shapes are the compatibility contract.
reference_written_manifest.days_affected_note: derived by the reference from PATH POSITION (two directory levels up, kept if digits). Rule 4a forbids that in a writer; the native writer takes days from the caller. Read-compat still applies to manifests already written this way.

hash_source_directory_discriminating.note: THE case the first oracle could not see. sorted(path.rglob('*')) orders Path objects by their PARTS TUPLE; collecting relpaths as strings and sorting is the obvious Rust port and gives a DIFFERENT digest. An Obsidian folder-note layout (Note.md beside Note/) is exactly this shape.

hash_source_directory_symlinks.note: is_file() FOLLOWS links: a symlink to a file is INCLUDED at its target's size; a symlinked DIRECTORY is NOT recursed. Rust walkdir defaults (follow_links(false) + file_type().is_file()) EXCLUDE the symlink-to-file and give a different digest.

windowed_source_hash.note: source_hash carries a #window: suffix whenever --date-from/--date-to are set. Owner journals already contain these. A native source_hash typed as a digest, or hex-validated on read, FAILS read-old.

reference_written_manifest_with_raw_rete.note: write_manifest emits raw_retention ONLY when non-None, so the manifest has 10 OR 11 keys. A struct reader built from the 10-key sample breaks on the body-source variant. Also: imported_at is datetime.now().isoformat() — NAIVE LOCAL TIME, no offset — so a reader demanding RFC3339-with-offset rejects every existing manifest.
